newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: NY archbishop backs UN chief despite Washington.
newsitem.headline: NY archbishop backs UN chief despite Washington.

text.p: Defying Washington, New York's Cardinal John O'Connor went out of his way to praise Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, who is seeking a second five-year term.

The Roman Catholic archbishop made his comments at a prayer service for U.N. delegates a week ago and distributed them on Monday. With the 73-year old Egyptian diplomat, a Coptic Christian, in the audience, O'Connor said: "It is my personal hope, Mr Boutros Boutros-Ghali, that I will have the privilege of serving you for a long time ahead. I thank you for what you have done."
O'Connor said he wanted to express his personal gratitude to "a man who I consider to be profoundly sensitive to the moral and spiritual issues of world affairs."

"He is a man with whom I have personally spoken, a man who has impressed me with a decency, with an integrity, with a true concern for the human person. ... He is explictly and concretely interested in the human person as made in the image and likeness of God."

The Clinton administration has vowed to block Boutros-Ghali from a second term when his current post expires at the end of the year. And Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole rarely misses an opportunity to accuse the world body of trying to usurp U.S. prerogatives, taking delight in stretching out every syllable of Boutros-Ghali's unusual name.

The archbishop said the world would be in "worse condition than it currently is" without the United Nations, adding that "the probability of all-out war would have become an actuality many, many years ago."
